doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

title: Naming the Rosanna lick and its ghosted note
summary: Rowe scats the Rosanna lick; Hey explains the ghosted note that makes it swing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I want you to see if you can name this lick.
Yeah uh oh because I have to try to vocalize it, okay? [scats]

So that’s the “Rosanna” lick. And there is a note in there that most people don’t know. It’s [scats] all — there’s a ghosted note in [scats] E ghosted in there [scats]. And that’s why it sounds like that because you get that ghost and then you get the second part of the lick [scats]. Where if you just went [scats] that doesn’t swing as well.
Yeah so Dan Fornero was on a session the other day and he sang that [scats]. And I said, “You know there’s this ghosted note.” And he goes, “No!” I said, “Yeah.”
Well I used to have to play that on a synthesizer in a band and believe me, I didn’t get the ghosted note.
